candidates.statement: MLPerf Tiny v0.5 specifies four benchmarks (keyword spotting, visual wake words, image classification, anomaly detection), each with one dataset, one MCU-sized reference model, and one numeric quality target.
Each benchmark's published quality target sits a small, consistent margin below its reference model's own measured accuracy/AUC, to absorb cross-platform quantization and rounding differences.
candidates.quote: To accommodate minor differences in quantization and various other optimizations, we set the quality target to 85% top-1 accuracy.

candidates.statement: The framework measures latency and energy as the median of five repeated runs (>=10s/>=10 iterations each) and accuracy as a single full-validation-set pass, gated by a minimum-accuracy validity check.

The closed division fixes dataset, model, and quality target and allows only post-training quantization; the open division allows changing dataset, training, and model but drops the mandatory accuracy bar and requires documenting every deviation.

The first submission round (v0.5, June 2021) produced 5 submissions spanning both divisions and 5 distinct hardware/software categories (ARM MCU, RISC-V MCU, a general-purpose SBC with a software toolchain, a dedicated NN accelerator, and an FPGA via HLS).

This diversity across division, hardware class, and software stack in a single first round is consistent with the modular reference-implementation design letting submitters at different layers of the deployment stack each demonstrate a distinct advantage while remaining comparable within the closed division.
candidates.quote: the benchmark suite was able to accommodate this diverse set of goals due to its modular design.

candidates.statement: Across the five v0.5 submissions, INT-8 was the most common numeric format, ML frameworks ranged from open interpreters to hardware-specific compilers, and measured device power ranged from microwatts to watts.
No v0.5 submission modified the training dataset, unlike a broader contemporary trend toward data-centric ML development.
CoreMark does not profile full programs or represent ML inference workloads.
MLMark uses real ML workloads but needs GB-scale memory (too large for MCUs) and has no power measurement.
MLPerf's ML-inference suite plans power measurement but currently excludes MCUs and other resource-constrained platforms.
None of CoreMark, MLMark, or MLPerf Inference jointly measures ML-inference accuracy, latency, and energy on MCU-class hardware with a reproducible methodology -- the gap MLPerf Tiny targets.
candidates.quote: there is a clear and distinct need for a TinyML benchmark that caters to the unique needs of ML workloads, makes power a first-class citizen and prescribes a methodology that suits TinyML.

candidates.statement: The benchmarks are already reused as standard TinyML research tasks and as public projects on a third-party development platform.
Future rounds should widen coverage to new application domains while keeping a stable long-term subset for tracking progress.
Future versions aim to widen the benchmark's scope to include pre-processing/streaming behavior.
Future reference suites may add architectures beyond FC/CNN, e.g. RNNs.

not_promoted.reason: societal risk/benefit reflection (E015) is framed by the authors as a general statement about the TinyML field, not a testable research claim about the benchmark itself -- kept as evidence cited directly in Discussion, without a claim ID.
